cues.zh: “‘早上好！’比尔博说，他是真心实意的。
cues.en: “‘Good morning!’ said Bilbo, and he meant it.

cues.zh: “‘你是什么意思？’甘道夫说。
cues.en: “‘What do you mean?’ Gandalf said.

cues.zh: “‘你是希望我有个美好的早晨，
cues.en: “‘Do you wish me a good morning,

cues.zh: “还是说不管我想不想，这都是个美好的早晨；
cues.en: “or mean that it is a good morning whether I want it or not;

cues.zh: “还是说你今天早上感觉很好；还是说这是个适合变好的早晨？’
cues.en: “or that you feel good this morning; or that it is a morning to be good on?’

cues.zh: “‘全都是，’比尔博说。
cues.en: “‘All of them at once,’ said Bilbo.

cues.zh: “‘你用‘早上好’来表达的东西可真多啊！’甘道夫说。”
cues.en: “‘What a lot of things you do use good morning for!’ said Gandalf.”

cues.zh: 甘道夫在那段对话中固执地忽略了一点，
cues.en: What Gandalf is stubbornly ignoring in that conversation,

cues.zh: 因为一个在中土世界生活了三千年的巫师
cues.en: because there’s no way that a wizard who’s lived in Middle Earth for 3,000 years

cues.zh: 不可能不理解“早上好”——
cues.en: doesn’t understand “good morning” --

cues.zh: 但不管怎样，他固执忽略的是，“早上好”这个说法
cues.en: but anyway, what he’s stubbornly ignoring is that the phrase “good morning”

cues.zh: 通常根本不传递信息。
cues.en: doesn’t usually convey information at all.

cues.zh: 相反，它起到的是社交功能。
cues.en: Instead, it serves a social function.

cues.zh: 它是一种问候。
cues.en: It is a greeting.

cues.zh: 这类表达被称为“寒暄语”。
cues.en: Expressions like this are called “phatic expressions”.

cues.zh: 这些短语中，语义信息
cues.en: They’re phrases where the semantic information

cues.zh: 远不如语用信息重要。
cues.en: is much less important than the pragmatic information.

cues.zh: 而且通常与礼貌有关。
cues.en: And generally, it’s to do with politeness.

cues.zh: “How are you”、“How's it going”和“Hello”都是短语，
cues.en: “How are you”, “How's it going” and “Hello” are all phrases

cues.zh: 由不同的词组成，但意思大致相同，
cues.en: that are made up of different words but mean approximately the same thing,

cues.zh: 以至于你可以相当互换地使用它们，
cues.en: to the point that you can switch them up fairly interchangeably,

cues.zh: 只要语气合适，而且你习惯了它们。
cues.en: as long as they're tonally appropriate and you're used to them.

cues.zh: 如果你是身处英国的美国人，
cues.en: If you’re an American in Britain,

cues.zh: 被问候“you alright?”可能会让你很不适应。
cues.en: it might be quite jarring to be asked “you alright?” as a greeting.

cues.zh: 对许多北美人来说，“are you alright”不是寒暄语，
cues.en: For many North Americans, “are you alright” is not a phatic expression,

cues.zh: 所以“Are you all right?”表达的是真切的关心。
cues.en: so “Are you all right?” expresses genuine concern.

cues.zh: 而且，很可能不是“you alright?”，而只是“y'arigh?”。
cues.en: Also, it probably won’t be “you alright?”, it’ll just be “y'arigh?”.

cues.zh: 反过来也一样：“What's up?”也是如此。对大多数英国人来说，这是表达关心，
cues.en: The other way around: applies to “What's up?”. For most Britons it’s an expression of concern,

cues.zh: 而不是问候：在英式英语中它不是寒暄语。
cues.en: not a greeting: it’s not phatic in British English.

cues.zh: 寒暄语会随时间变化。
cues.en: Phatic expressions change with time.

cues.zh: 你好吗？
cues.en: “How do you do?”

cues.zh: 逐渐演变成“Howdy do”，再变成“howdy”，
cues.en: eroded over time to “Howdy do” and then “howdy”,

cues.zh: 但对大多数现代听众来说，这些说法都显得过时又正式。
cues.en: but all those sound dated and formal to most modern listeners.

cues.zh: 这种变化一直在发生！
cues.en: And these changes happen all the time!

cues.zh: 现在人们通常用“no problem”来回应“thank you”。
cues.en: It’s now usual to reply to ”thank you” with “no problem.”

cues.zh: 但这有点争议，因为对一些人（通常是年长者）来说，
cues.en: But that’s a bit contentious because for some, usually older, folks

cues.zh: “no problem”不算寒暄，而且不礼貌：
cues.en: “no problem” is not phatic and it’s impolite:

cues.zh: 应该用“you're welcome”才对。
cues.en: it should be “you’re welcome” instead.

cues.zh: 而在许多年轻人看来，这句话同样不礼貌！
cues.en: Which, to many younger folks, also sounds impolite!

cues.zh: 只要语言还在变化，这种代际差异就会一直存在。
cues.en: We’re going to have these generational differences as long as language continues to change.

cues.zh: 那我们为什么还要费心使用寒暄语呢？
cues.en: So why do we bother with phatic expressions at all?

cues.zh: 为什么直接跳到真正想说的话就显得无礼呢？
cues.en: Why is it rude to just immediately jump to what you actually want to say?

cues.zh: 嗯，问候是一种认可对方的方式，
cues.en: Well, greetings are a way to either acknowledge another person,

cues.zh: 通过建立关系来开启对话，
cues.en: to initiate conversation by establishing a relationship,

cues.zh: 或者它是一种口头上的握手，确保大家都在注意。
cues.en: or they're a verbal sort of handshake to make sure everyone’s paying attention.

cues.zh: 根据我们选择的寒暄语，
cues.en: Depending on the phatic expression we choose,

cues.zh: 我们可以传达出层级关系或意图。
cues.en: we can convey a hierarchical relation or intent.

cues.zh: 我们可以用它们来道别。
cues.en: We can use them for saying goodbye.

cues.zh: 还有一些用于“反馈回应”的寒暄语，
cues.en: There are also phatic expressions for “backchanneling”,

cues.zh: 也就是我们用来表示自己在积极倾听的方式。
cues.en: which is how we express that we are actively listening.

cues.zh: 它们起到语用功能，表明你确实在听，
cues.en: Those serve the pragmatic function of demonstrating that, yes, you are listening,

cues.zh: 而且此刻你并不想成为说话的那个人。你不会去打断。
cues.en: and that you don't desire to be the one talking at the moment. You're not going to interrupt.

cues.zh: 这就是为什么反馈回应常常出现在句子末尾；
cues.en: This is why backchannels often happen at the end of sentences;

cues.zh: 它们是听者意识到自己此时可以插话，
cues.en: they are the listener recognizing that they could jump into the conversation at this point,

cues.zh: 但却选择继续倾听。
cues.en: but they are choosing to continue to listen instead.

cues.zh: 它们的普遍程度因语言和文化而异，
cues.en: Their prevalence varies from language to language, and culture to culture,

cues.zh: 这可能导致误解。
cues.en: which can lead to misunderstandings.

cues.zh: 在日本，附和应答如此普遍，以至于外国商务人士
cues.en: In Japanese, backchanneling is so ubiquitous that foreign businesspeople

cues.zh: 有时会把它误认为是在表示赞同，以为对方在说
cues.en: sometimes mistake it for agreement, and think that people are saying

cues.zh: “好，我同意”，而不是“好，我明白你的意思，继续说”。
cues.en: “okay, I agree” and not “okay, I understand you, carry on”.

cues.zh: 并非所有人都同等看待所有的寒暄表达。
cues.en: Not all phatic expressions are treated equally by everyone.

cues.zh: 所以要留意它们。它们无处不在。
cues.en: So look out for them. They are everywhere.

cues.zh: 想的话，可以随意把玩它们，用些不寻常的……只是……
cues.en: Play around with them and use unusual ones if you want… just…

cues.zh: 别当甘道夫。
cues.en: don’t be Gandalf.

cues.zh: 我的合著者Gretchen McCulloch的新书《Because Internet》
cues.en: My co-author Gretchen McCulloch’s new book Because Internet

cues.zh: 其中谈到，我们为何对电子邮件中的寒暄表达如此焦虑：
cues.en: includes a bit on why we stress out so much about phatic expressions in email:

cues.zh: 邮件开头该用“Hi”、“Dear Name”，还是完全不同的别的什么。
cues.en: whether you should start that message with “Hi” or “Dear Name” or something else entirely.

cues.zh: 简介里有她这本书的链接！
cues.en: There are links to her book in the description!
